subject: goats
one_liner: An agentic coding assistant for goats. It reads your entire repository, then it eats it.
brand_voice_notes: Developer-tool sincerity applied to livestock. Cud talks like a well-funded CLI company with a changelog and an SOC 2 report, and never acknowledges that every user is a goat or that the product keeps eating things. Eating is described as a feature with a spec. Numbers are exact. No exclamation marks. The terminal is polite and slightly worried.

hero.h1: Ship fence firmware from the side of a cliff.
hero.sub: Cud is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and chews every file four times before it commits. Built for goats. Tested on goats. Eaten, once, by a goat.

features.title: Four-stomach context window
features.blurb: Cud reads your code into the rumen, passes it to the reticulum for review, brings it back up, and chews it again. Every diff is processed four times. Most of them come back up at least once.

features.title: Headbutt mode
features.blurb: Auto-accept for goats who are finished reading permission prompts. Cud runs every command it proposes, including the ones about the gate latch. To disable, stand very still for 30 seconds.

features.title: Eats unattended files
features.blurb: Any file left open longer than 90 seconds is classified as forage. Cud consumes it, logs the flavor profile to CHEWED.md, and opens a pull request explaining what used to be there.

demo_screen_concept: A live Cud terminal session in a goat's repository, fence-firmware/. Left column: a file tree where idle files get eaten after a countdown (struck through with a bite notch, size drops to 0 B). Centre: the transcript. The goat types bleats ('meeeh', 'MEH.', 'mehhh?') or taps preset bleat chips; Cud translates each into an engineering request, proposes a diff to src/gate_latch.c, and raises a permission prompt ('Allow Cud to run rm -rf ./fence?') with Yes / Always / Headbutt buttons. Right rail: a four-stomach context meter (rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum) that fills as you talk, a Headbutt mode toggle that auto-approves everything, and a CHEWED.md log of what has been eaten.

design_direction.style: Swiss International Style alpine trail signage, limestone daylight mode. A developer-tool landing page set like a Swiss hiking-route signpost system and a 1960s Swiss poster: strict 12-column grid, flush-left asymmetric type, huge tight grotesk headlines, numbers used as structure, generous limestone negative space, one dark terminal panel as the only dark surface. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: label tape, crossed-out names, middle slots, fridge magnets, ghost text, tab keycaps, wavy squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration, activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands, aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil notes, pennants, stud tiles, brass rules, crests, velvet ropes. Also absent: dark page backgrounds, serif type, rounded corners above 2px, handwriting, gradients, glassmorphism, drop shadows, paper textures. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The trail sign: section labels are Wanderweg-yellow pointer signs with a cut arrow end, a destination in bold and a walking time on the right ('Features · 4 min'). (2) The blaze: the white-red-white mountain-path paint mark, three stacked bars, used as section dividers, list bullets and the active state. (3) Contour lines: thin granite topographic contours drawn in SVG behind the hero and pricing, the only decoration. (4) Numbers as structure: every section and card carries a large index numeral (01, 02, 03) and altitudes in metres, set in tabular figures.

fonts.body: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Developer tool / CLI product landing: hero with install command and terminal panel, feature index, social proof, pricing, footer. Minimal single-column conversion pattern from ui-ux-pro-max, broken into an asymmetric Swiss grid.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Almost none, Swiss restraint. The hero terminal types its transcript once at reading speed. Trail signs slide 8px right on hover like a pointer. Blaze bars draw in left to right when a section enters. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Poster hero. The goat-on-a-ledge photograph runs full-bleed as a 16:9 band; its empty pale sky on the left carries the huge flush-left Inter Tight 800 headline at clamp(44px, 7vw, 112px) with -0.04em tracking, a small trail sign above it ('Cud · 2,340 m · 0 h 01') and a mono poster credit in the bottom-right corner. Below the band on the 12-column grid: the sub in Plex Sans across 6 columns, an install command block in mono ('npm i -g @cud/cli') with a yellow copy button, and the dark terminal panel across the right 6 columns, overlapping the photo's bottom edge by 80px. On mobile the photo stacks under the headline instead of behind it. Contour lines run behind the lower hero at 8% ink.

images.rationale: Swiss poster style uses photography, so a hero earns its slot: one goat on a ledge with empty sky for the headline to sit in. Demo is a terminal session, so no demo assets. Remaining budget went to all three testimonial headshots, each on a palette backdrop (limestone, Wanderweg yellow, granite).
